key_insight: Klear is a unified multi-task audio–video joint generation framework that combines architectural cross-modal alignment, targeted training objectives, and curated dense-caption data to substantially reduce audio–visual asynchrony and improve lip–speech alignment. It tackles unimodal degradation by enforcing stronger audio–visual correspondence and better generalization.
problem_solved: Addresses persistent issues in non-commercial audio–video generation—audio–visual asynchrony, poor lip–speech alignment, and unimodal degradation—caused by weak cross-modal modeling, limited generalization, and scarce high-quality dense-caption supervision.
method: Unified multi-task architecture that fuses audio and video streams with dedicated cross-attention/alignment modules to enforce temporal and semantic synchronization.

Targeted training strategy combining multi-task objectives (generation, lip-sync/alignment loss, contrastive A–V matching), curriculum learning, and multimodal augmentation to improve robustness and generalization.
Curated dense-caption dataset pipeline and synthetic alignment augmentation to expand high-quality paired audio–video supervision and reduce noisy/self-supervised artifacts.
impact: Makes audio–video generative models more reliable and synchronized for applications such as dubbing, virtual avatars, and content creation, while improving downstream performance and scalability through stronger cross-modal learning.

paper_title: Klear: Unified Multi-Task Audio-Video Joint Generation
